overview.description: Courchevel is an Omaha poker variant popular in France and the UK. Each player receives five hole cards and one community card is dealt face up before the first betting round. After that round, two more board cards complete the flop; then turn and river with betting after each. Players must use exactly two of their five hole cards with three board cards to make the best hand. Best hand wins the pot.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: France
Time Period: Late 20th century
Historical Development: Named after the Courchevel ski resort in the French Alps; reportedly invented by tourists. Commonly played at the Aviation Club de France in Paris (now closed).
Cultural Significance: Popular in France; spread to UK and other parts of Europe.
timeline: Late 20th century: Game invented at or named after Courchevel ski resort
Aviation Club de France: Main venue in Paris until closure
Modern Era: Played in France and UK; Hi-Low 8-or-better variety exists

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.
nullReasons.cultural: No specific cultural or regional significance documented beyond its origins.

setup.deck: Type: Standard 52-card deck. One deck. No jokers.
setup.dealing: Five hole cards each, dealt face down. One community card dealt face up before the first betting round. After that round, dealer burns one card and deals two more face up (three-card flop). Then turn (one card) and river (one card), with a burn before each. Betting after each street.

rules.objective: Make the best five-card hand using exactly two of your five hole cards and exactly three of the five board cards. Win the pot at showdown.
rules.gameplay: Deal five hole cards to each player and one community card face up. First betting round. Dealer burns one, deals two more board cards (flop). Second betting round. Turn card; third betting round. River card; fourth betting round. Showdown: active players show all five hole cards; best five-card hand using exactly two hole and three board wins the pot.
keyRules: Five hole cards; one board card before first betting, then flop (two more), turn, river.
Must use exactly two hole cards and three board cards.
Standard poker hand ranking. Pot Limit or other limits as agreed.

strategy.basic: Play hands that can make strong combinations with two cards from five; the exposed first board card gives extra information before the first betting round.
strategy.intermediate: Use the single exposed card to narrow ranges; position and starting hand selection matter; avoid hands that need three specific board cards.
strategy.advanced: Equity calculations with five hole cards and one known board card; blocker effects; pot control; adjust to Pot Limit or table stakes.
tips: Exactly two hole and three board cards; the first board card is visible before preflop betting.
More flexibility than 4-card Omaha; the early board card changes preflop strategy.
Courchevel Hi-Lo 8-or-better splits the pot between high and low.

fold.description: Forfeit the hand and give up any claim to the pot; cards are discarded face-down.
fold.constraints: Legal during any betting round when it is your turn to act.

check.description: Decline to bet and pass action to the next player; no chips are put in the pot.
check.constraints: Legal only when no bet has been made in the current round (or you are facing zero to call).

call.description: Match the current bet to stay in the hand.
call.constraints: Legal when facing a bet; must match the full amount of the current bet or all-in.

bet.description: Put chips into the pot; in Pot Limit the maximum is the current pot size; in No Limit any amount up to stack.
bet.constraints: Legal when no bet has been made in the current round (or you are first to act and can open).

raise.description: Increase the current bet; must be at least the minimum raise (often the size of the previous bet or raise).
raise.constraints: Legal when facing a bet; must raise by at least the minimum; in Pot Limit maximum raise equals pot.

declare.reason: This game has no declare phase.

reveal_hand.description: Show all five hole cards at showdown; last aggressor shows first, then clockwise. Best five-card hand using exactly two hole and three board wins.
reveal_hand.constraints: Legal in showdown phase; active players must show all hole cards.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
